About the role

Would you like to be part of an ambitious Compliance team where you play a key role in ensuring that Saxo meets its regulatory obligations across all parts of the Information Communication Technology (ICT) organisation?

If so, this may be the right opportunity for you.

You will join the Prudential Oversight team within Group Compliance, Saxo's second line of defence function, based at our headquarters in Hellerup. The team oversees compliance risks across ICT, operational risk and data governance, supporting the business in meeting regulatory requirements, market standards and internal policies. Working closely with Compliance colleagues in Denmark and internationally, you will play a key role in strengthening compliance oversight across Saxo's technology organisation.

Your primary responsibility will be to conduct compliance oversight and monitoring across ICT areas regulated by DORA, including ICT risk management, incident management, business continuity and resilience testing, access management, critical functions and systems and third-party ICT service providers.

Depending on your profile, knowledge and experience, the role may also include compliance activities within operational risk, data quality and data governance.

As a team, we balance professionalism with a sense of humour and maintain an informal atmosphere where people enjoy coming to work.

Responsibilities

You will join an organisation where the foundation of the business is built on ICT and where platform availability is key to help clients get invested in the world. In the Prudential Oversight Compliance Team, ICT regulation is a core focus, and you will help us support Saxo in continuously driving this important area in a compliant direction.

Your main responsibilities will be to:

• 
Perform compliance risk assessments within the areas of ICT risks, operational risks and data risks, with a particular focus on DORA-related requirements

• 
Provide advice, challenge and compliance opinions to the business on regulatory requirements and compliance risks

• 
Conduct compliance monitoring activities, including follow-up and closure of recommendations

• 
Contribute to regular compliance reporting to the senior management of the bank

• 
Participate in developing Saxo’s compliance framework

• 
Collaborate closely with our Compliance Team in India

• 
Interact with the business across organisational levels and seniority

Your profile

We are looking for a colleague with solid experience working in ICT compliance, operational risk, data governance or technology risk management.

Most importantly, you have experience working with ICT requirements and legislation, ICT governance, risk assessments, and advisory work related to ICT requirements, and you are familiar with DORA or NIS2.

You may have gained this experience within a second line of defence compliance or risk function, a first line of defence risk or control role within financial services, internal or external audit, IT audit, consultancy or another highly regulated industry. Experience with operational risk and data governance is considered an advantage.

Moreover, we are looking for someone who is detail-oriented, can work independently while taking an active role in teamwork, and enjoys collaborating with colleagues and stakeholders across the entire organisation.

It is an advantage if you thrive in an environment with constant change, bring a positive and curious mindset to work, and do not buy into the word ‘cannot’.

You must possess strong stakeholder management skills and use your communication skills to ensure positive collaboration and progress in joint tasks. We are looking for a colleague who always brings a positive attitude when liaising with the business.

Please note! International applicants are encouraged to apply. To help us understand your circumstances, we kindly ask candidates currently based outside Denmark to include a brief summary of their relocation plans and expected timeframe for relocating to Denmark.

jobs.description:
Are you motivated by valuation and financial modelling? Do you enjoy turning complex numbers into meaningful insights? Join our team and help leading corporates, institutions, and financial investors solve complex challenges and make smarter decisions. Together, we create impactful financial solutions that drive value for our clients.

About the role

As an associate in our Valuation & Financial Modelling team, (part of our Corporate Finance practice), you will work closely with leading Danish corporates, investment funds, banks and other financial institutions. From day one, you will handle meaningful tasks, work together with specialists in different fields across the world, and receive practical training from experienced colleagues. We believe in learning by doing, supporting each other, and developing solid knowledge of valuation and financial modelling while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

You will have the opportunity to:

• 
Build and review investment models for large-scale infrastructure and renewable energy projects, working closely together with investors, corporates, and banks (our clients).

• 
Deliver independent valuations that support M&A transactions, management incentive programs, and complex legal or tax cases, where your analysis will guide decision-making.

• 
Contribute to our renewable energy M&A focus, helping design value-driven solutions in one of the most dynamic sectors of today’s economy.

Perks of joining Valuations and Financial Modelling

You will join a motivated and collaborative team where you get to work closely with experienced colleagues from day one. We combine a clear professional focus with an informal and supportive team culture, where we learn from each other, share knowledge, and have fun along the way.

What makes our team different is the opportunity to work on complex and important financial challenges that require both analytical thinking and commercial understanding. You will get practical experience with real client challenges, contribute to important decisions and see the impact of your work, rather than simply supporting from the sidelines.

We invest in your development from the start. You will receive targeted financial modelling training, alongside training in a range of other relevant technical topics, giving you the practical tools and knowledge needed to build a solid foundation for a career within the team.

If you are curious, motivated, and enjoy leading your own work, while being part of a team that supports and challenges you, you will find plenty of opportunities to grow with us.

About you, our new team member

You enjoy working with people and building strong relationships with clients, colleagues, and cross-functional teams. You thrive in a collaborative environment where knowledge sharing, teamwork, and mutual support are valued. At the same time, you appreciate a positive and social workplace where professional excellence and having fun go hand in hand.

More specifically, we are looking for someone who:

• 
Has a keen interest in numerical and logical reasoning.

• 
Has a genuine interest in addressing complex financial challenges.

• 
Is proficient in Excel and similar analytical tools.

• 
Has a solid sense of ownership and an ability to work independently on assigned tasks.

• 
Has an interest in working with external stakeholders.

• 
Has an interest in igniting your own career potential within a service line committed to growth.

• 
Communicates confidently and professionally in English, both verbally and in writing.

• 
Holds or are expected to complete a relevant master's degree before Autumn 2027.

KPMG Advisory Academy

As part of your development, you will join the KPMG Advisory Academy, a 14-month development program designed to give you a solid foundation for your consulting career. Through a combination of professional training, personal development, networking opportunities, and practical client experience, you will build key consulting skills while expanding your network across KPMG Advisory.

Want to learn more about the KPMG Advisory Academy and how it supports your development from day one? Read more about the Advisory Academy here.

Are you ready to become part of KPMG? Send your application today!

The application deadline is 15 November, but we review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the process earlier - so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Interviews are expected to take place in November and December.

What accomplishment are you most proud of and why?

Join our digital transformation and shape end-2-end build-in quality.

We are looking for an experienced and proactive QA, Test and Release Manager to lead quality assurance, testing and release management for a strategic SaaS implementation. About the role

You will take ownership of the end-to-end quality, test and release approach across an iterative delivery landscape. Your focus will be to embed quality early, create effective quality gates and coordinate the people, environments and decisions required for successful releases. You will combine hands-on delivery leadership with clear governance and confident stakeholder management.

You will be a trusted adviser to programme and product leadership, providing fact-based release-readiness assessments and clear go/no-go recommendations. Success in the role requires close collaboration across business and technology teams, including teams in different countries and external suppliers.

Your responsibilities

• 
Develop, implement and continuously improve the QA strategy, test strategy and integrated test plans.

• 
Define test scope, coverage, entry and exit criteria, quality gates and release-readiness standards.

• 
Coordinate functional, integration, regression, user acceptance and relevant non-functional testing across multiple teams.

• 
Build and maintain the release roadmap and calendar, aligning delivery scope, dependencies, environments and stakeholder capacity.

• 
Coordinate deployments, staging activities, cutover readiness, rollback plans and post-release follow-up.

• 
Lead defect management and triage, ensuring clear ownership, prioritisation, resolution and transparent risk assessment.

• 
Plan and facilitate test status, release-readiness and go/no-go meetings, providing evidence-based recommendations to management.

• 
Collaborate closely with software suppliers, product teams, developers, architects, business analysts, testers and business representatives.

• 
Provide timely, concise and accurate reporting on test progress, coverage, defect trends, risks and release confidence.

• 
Drive continuous improvement of testing practices, tools, automation opportunities and CI/CD ways of working.

About you

• 
Obtained relevant certifications like ISTQB, CSTM, CSTP or similar

• 
Substantial experience in QA, test management and release management in complex technology programmes or product environments

• 
Demonstrated ability to create and execute test strategies and test plans across multiple teams, systems and integrations.

• 
Strong knowledge of the software development lifecycle, agile delivery, CI/CD, release governance and environment management.

• 
Experience with SaaS implementations and collaboration with external software providers.

• 
Solid understanding of functional and non-functional testing, UAT, regression testing and defect management.

• 
Experience using test and delivery management tools such as Jira or comparable platforms.

• 
Strong analytical skills and the judgement to translate test evidence into clear risk and release recommendations.

• 
Excellent communication, facilitation and stakeholder-management skills in English.

What will help you succeed

• 
You take ownership, create structure and maintain momentum in a complex environment.

• 
You communicate difficult messages clearly and constructively, including when quality evidence does not support a release.

• 
You balance attention to detail with an understanding of the wider business and delivery context.

• 
You build trust across organisational boundaries and are comfortable influencing senior stakeholders.

• 
You promote a quality-first mindset while remaining pragmatic and focused on business outcomes.

What we offer

You will join a high-ranked digital transformation programme with the opportunity to establish strong quality and release practices, influence important delivery decisions and work with experienced colleagues across business and technology. The role offers broad exposure, meaningful responsibility and the chance to improve how complex solutions are delivered into production. We are located in Birkerød and expect physical presence at least two days weekly (Tuesdays and Thursdays).

Interested, then do not hesitate to apply or reach out

Please submit your application and resume. We will review continuously, so apply as soon as possible. For questions, contact Bent Thomsen Munthe, Principal Program Manager at bmunt@nordania.dk or by phone on +45 5156 8097. We are looking forward to receiving your application.

jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer – IoT Platform, Load and Energy Management
jobs.description:
🚀 About the role

We're looking for a senior software engineer who writes solid, reliable code and wants that code to control real hardware. At FLEXECHARGE, our HARMON-E platform manages load and energy for EV charging operators across Europe. Part of it runs at the edge, on an industrial PC next to chargers, batteries and solar inverters, and connected to the interfaces DSOs use to curtail load.

You'll build and maintain the TypeScript microservices that talk to those devices and turn their data into decisions. This is not a web-app role. It's software engineering for systems where the other side is physical, stateful and often unreliable.

⚡ What is special about this role

It sits where two worlds meet:

• 
Web and cloud toolchain: TypeScript, Docker, MQTT, Azure, Kubernetes.

• 
Operational technology and system integration: talking to real chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus and OCPP, running at the edge on an industrial PC.

Your code won't only talk to clean APIs in a data centre. It runs on site, next to real peripheral devices, and has to keep doing its job when those devices and the networks between them don't behave as expected.

We recognize that TypeScript is not typically used for edge computing or hardware interfacing. This is why we're looking for a strong software engineer who is interested in learning new techniques and applications, as well as applying their technical skills in novel ways.

🛠️ What you'll do

• 
Write and maintain a combination of TypeScript microservices and the business logic behind them: control algorithms, scheduling and decision-making, not just plumbing.

• 
Build and extend device drivers for chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus TCP, using our existing driver services as a starting point.

• 
Work with OCPP, which our platform already supports, as you ramp up.

• 
Run services in containers at the edge and connect them through MQTT and pub/sub messaging to our cloud backend.

• 
Profile and optimise software on edge hardware, where hardware resources are constrained.

• 
Help shape the long-term move of performance-critical services to compiled languages.

• 
Mentor and pair with colleagues on integrations and software craft.

🤔 Why compiled languages, if we write TypeScript?

It may sound odd, so here's the reasoning. Today the majority of our edge stack is TypeScript, and you'll develop in it from day one. Over time we want to move selected services, such as device interfaces and performance-critical paths, to a compiled language while keeping them part of the same stack.

To do that well, you need to understand both sides: the TypeScript services as they are now, and the concepts of memory, types and performance that compiled languages force you to think about. In our experience, it's much easier to go from a compiled language to a scripting environment than the other way around. So if you're a Go, C, C++, Rust or similar developer who is happy to work in TypeScript (or happy to learn), you're exactly who we're looking for.

✅ Must-have

• 
3–5+ years of professional software development, with strong software and engineering fundamentals.

• 
Professional experience in a compiled language (for example Go, C, C++, Rust, C# or Java).

• 
Proficiency in a scripting language, ideally TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript or Python, or a clear willingness to become productive in TypeScript quickly.

• 
Experience writing business logic with stateful calculations and operations, which can self-heal and recover gracefully.

• 
Comfort with asynchronous and event-driven systems that talk to unreliable external components or peripheral devices.

💡 Strongly preferred (but we'll teach it)

• 
Hands-on device or protocol integration: Modbus, serial interfaces, Ethernet/TCP-IP or comparable.

• 
Containerised applications. Docker, Docker Compose or Kubernetes are ideal, but any container technology counts.

• 
Pub/sub and distributed systems, ideally MQTT or another IoT messaging protocol, and an understanding of their reliability concerns.

• 
Working within constrained systems, including profiling software to find where CPU or memory limits bite.

🎁 Bonus, not a requirement

• 
OCPP experience.

• 
Energy, EV charging or power-systems domain knowledge.

• 
Edge deployment experience.

If you don't have these, apply anyway. Strong fundamentals and the right mindset matter more. 💪

🚫 This role is probably not for you if

• 
Your experience is mainly frontend or request/response web apps, with no compiled-language background.

• 
You prefer to stay in one language and aren't interested in working in TypeScript.

• 
You want a pure firmware or PLC role without writing higher-level services.

• 
You don't enjoy debugging the messy cases where hardware doesn't behave as documented.

🌆 What is it like to work at FLEXECHARGE?

• 
Our office is in Frederiksberg: bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday.

• 
You're covered with pension contributions.

• 
Lunch is served on-site, and it's delicious, healthy and nutritious.

• 
We enjoy each other's company outside work too, with Friday bars, company events and team-building activities within each team.

• 
You'll have opportunities for individual development.

🤝 Our interview process

Here's roughly what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• 
A first conversation (about 30 minutes) with our recruiter. You'll get a feel for the role, ask whatever's on your mind, and we'll both get a sense of whether this is worth pursuing further.

• 
Time with the team: a conversation with Kasper, our Head of Architecture & Systems, and Robert, our CTO.

• 
A technical stage: one or more interviews with the team, which may include a case exercise and follow-up discussions. These can take place remotely or at our office.

• 
A conversation with Max, our CEO, alongside someone else from the team.

Hiring carefully matters to us. We want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you.

📍 Location & practical details

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen. Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• 
We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

• 
We do not offer relocation services.

🔐 Data privacy (GDPR)

Applications for this role are processed exclusively through The Hub (thehub.io), our recruitment platform, in accordance with their privacy policy and applicable GDPR requirements. As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarise interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process.

For more information or questions please contact us at iva@flexecharge.com

Working at

FLEXECHARGE

FLEXECHARGE is a cleantech scale-up which offers a powerful load & energy management platform, as a SaaS, to help Charge Point Operators (ex: Clever, eOn, etc.) to optimise their charging operations & business. Our mission is accelerate green mobility through our Smart Charging solutions that make charging faster, greener and cheaper. Our vision is to integrate charging infrastructures better with the grid supply and the ever more volatile & growing production of renewable energy. We want to connect electric vehicles with the grid in a whole new way. By seeing electric vehicles not as a risk for our supply grid, but as a crucial asset for the transition towards 100% renewable energy. We do this through constant innovation of new smart charging features which will make us the preferred partner for EV infrastructure owners, developers, and operators.

Essential qualifications include:

• An academic degree in veterinary medicine, pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutical sciences or another relevant life-science discipline.

• Several years of experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology drug development, including experience with small-molecule development.

• At least three years of experience in nonclinical project management or a comparable cross-functional drug development role.

Useful, but not essential: A PhD in a relevant discipline. Equivalent, relevant industry experience will also be considered.

What you’ll do

• Lead nonclinical project management for a portfolio of small-molecule projects, from lead candidate selection through clinical development and towards market.

• Coordinate work across toxicology, safety pharmacology, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, bioanalysis and related development disciplines.

• Establish and maintain integrated project plans covering timelines, budgets, risks, dependencies, resources, and key deliverables.

• Bring teams together to identify and resolve issues, maintain momentum, and prepare projects for important development milestones.

You will work closely with nonclinical development teams, external partners and specialists across toxicology, safety pharmacology, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics, bioanalysis and related functions. jobs.occupation: Project manager for international research projects
jobs.description:
Are you enthusiastic about making a difference to large societal challenges such as green transition of energy, materials and food systems?

Do you have experience with research project management, funding administration and project development? 

Do you know your way around a Horizon Europe project and do you enjoy being the person who keeps a large international consortium on track?

Do you thrive in a dynamic working environment, with multiple external and internal stakeholders?

Then we might be looking for you!

At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering at Aarhus University, we are busy conducting research on a broad range of topics related to green transition, sustainability and health. Our portfolio of EU-funded projects is growing, and we are therefore looking for an experienced EU project manager with international experience who can drive development and execution of international projects in close collaboration with researchers, external partners and the department’s Partnerships and External Relations team.

Expected starting date and duration
The position is a two-year fixed-term position starting on 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job descripton
At Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, we are experiencing an increase in externally funded, international research and innovation projects. As project manager you will play a key role in managing and coordinating the department’s participation in such projects, in particular large Horizon Europe projects with multiple partners, where our department has a leading role 

Working closely with the scientific coordinator, you will:

• Act as the day-to-day operational point of contact for the consortium. 
• Drive the coordination machinery: Track deliverables, milestones and risks, chase and quality-assure partner contributions.
• Prepare periodic/final reporting, and coordinate financial reporting with partners and with the administrative and financial experts in AU’s central research support office.
• Plan and run consortium, General Assembly and review meetings: Agendas, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
• Maintain the Consortium Agreement and support obligations on data management, ethics, dissemination, exploitation and communication.
In addition to this, you will:

• Support the department’s wider portfolio of international projects, being work package or task manager where relevant.
• Provide guidance and support to the development of new European grant proposals and the building of new consortia.
• Participate in and help organise externally oriented activities and events.
• Help shape the department’s way of working around externally funded projects, so that good practice is developed and shared.
The role is vested in the department’s Partnerships and External Relations team. The team supports our researchers within multiple aspects of externally funded research collaborations - from strategy development, visibility, partnership and project development to execution of complex projects. We are continuously developing our way of working to support increased activity level and creation of impact.

Qualifications
We are looking for someone who combines hands-on experience of EU project execution with the ability to work comfortably alongside researchers in a technical field.

Technical qualifications:

• Academic degree in a relevant field (e.g., technical sciences, international relations etc.).
• Experience with the day-to-day management of Horizon Europe or Horizon 2020 projects; including reporting, deliverable and milestone tracking.
• Experience of working with international research consortia and of coordinating contributions from partners in several countries.
• The ability to engage with technical content well enough to quality-assure deliverables and to discuss the work with researchers on their own terms.
Qualifications we regard as an advantage:

• Experience from the coordinator side of an EU project, rather than as a beneficiary partner only.
• Experience with proposal development, grant writing and consortium building.
• Familiarity with research areas related to the green transition; for example bioresources, biotechnology, chemical or environmental engineering.
• Familiarity with EU financial rules, cost eligibility and audit requirements.
Personal qualifications:

• Excellent communication skills, with fluency in English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
• Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders and priorities effectively
• Service-minded attitude, flexibility, and a collaborative approach to working in a team
• Ability to travel internationally as needed (few times per year). 
Who we are
At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering we focus on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering etc. more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food.

At the department, we educate BEng, BSc and MSc graduates in engineering for Danish society.

Read more about the department and sections here:
https://bce.au.dk/en/research/key-areas-in-research-and-development

Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering offers:

• Opportunity to contribute to solutions of crucial importance to society and industry
• The possibility of being part of a dynamic research environment in rapid development
• An exciting, cross-disciplinary environment with strong external partnerships with industrial and academic partners in Denmark and abroad
• A workplace characterized by professionalism, trust and healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work Gustav Wieds Vej 10D, 8000 Aarhus, Denmark and the area of employment is Aarhus University, Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Deputy head of department, Thomas Lundgaard, +45 29 16 31 35 / thomas.lundgaard@bce.au.dk

Application deadline
9 November 2026.

Formalities and salary range
You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. For the right candidate, there will be an opportunity to be appointed as a Special Consultant, with remuneration in accordance with Appendix 4 of the collective agreement.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.
